verdicts.trueWording: There are other things, just offstage, that the reader knows will
verdicts.note: Live raw page brightweavings.com/nyrsf_halasz/ (HTTP 200, 72KB). Quote is verbatim in GGK's answer beginning 'Well, I'll tell you about the splitting' — the paragraph about Crispin's journey, immediately after 'The book describes the arc of that journey and ends at the finish of it.' Page header confirms Peter Halasz interviewed GGK for the New York Review of Science Fiction during 2000. Every limb (Kay speaking; about Sailing to Sarantium; things left offstage the reader knows will happen) is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: FIONAVAR, a land of undetermined location
verdicts.note: Live raw page brightweavings.com/dictionary/ (HTTP 200, 57KB). Quote opens the entry, exactly as the claim's 'first line of the entry' says. Page states it is the entry on Fionavar in The Dictionary of Imaginary Places by Alberto Manguel and Gianni Guadalupi, reprinted with permission.

verdicts.trueWording: (designed by the gifted T’Varen in the reign of Thallason)
verdicts.note: Same page. The parenthesis sits in the Cathal/Larai Rigal paragraph, attached to the walled gardens of the Summer Palace — a built work credited to a named maker (T’Varen) and a named reign (Thallason) inside a parenthesis, as claimed. Curly apostrophe in T’Varen matches the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Access to the Godwood and the tree is strictly controlled
verdicts.note: Same page, paragraph on the Mõrnirwood/Godwood west of Paras Derval, which houses the Summer Tree. Stated flatly as a standing condition, continuing 'and the casual traveller is unlikely in the extreme to have occasion or opportunity to go there' — no scene is narrated there, so the 'administrative fact rather than a scene' limb holds.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'rather than narrating it' — the entry declares the prehistory hazy and then does narrate it, in the same paragraph and the two that follow
verdicts.note: Same page. The quotation is verbatim and opens its paragraph. But the declaration is not used in place of narration: the same sentence run continues 'Originally there appear to have been only two peoples… These were followed by the lios alfar and the Dwarves', then 'Many years later Men arrived on the Plain', then a full paragraph narrating the Bael Rangat with Conary's death in battle, Colan's succession, Revor's Dalrei, Rakoth's binding and the five wardstones. The hazy-prehistory limb is supported; the contrastive limb is not.

verdicts.trueWording: it is a matter of some dispute which race came first
verdicts.note: Same page, in the paragraph beginning 'Fionavar’s prehistory is hazy', of the lios alfar and the Dwarves. The entry leaves the question open and never returns to settle it, so both limbs (records the dispute; does not settle it) hold.

verdicts.trueWording: neither has offered an account of what they saw there
verdicts.note: Same page, paragraph on the Dwarves of Banir Lõk and Banir Tal and Calor Diman. The page reads 'Other than the Dwarves themselves only two people — Loren Silvercloak… and Kimberly Ford… have been permitted to enter the meadow of the Crystal Lake, and neither has offered an account of what they saw there.' The 'only two' limb is the page's own wording (Dwarves excepted as residents).

verdicts.trueWording: There have been reports of a lessening of this sentient forest’s
verdicts.note: Same page, paragraph on Pendaran, the Great Wood. Continues 'antipathy to intruders of all kinds, but pending confirmation of this the traveller is advised to stay well clear of what may still be a very dangerous area' — supplying both the unconfirmed-report hedge and the consequent advice.

verdicts.trueWording: There are sixty-five members of the Rector’s Council as of this
verdicts.note: Live raw page brightweavings.com/review-by-bill-capossere-for-fantasy-literature/ (HTTP 200, 56KB). The quotation opens the block quotation that directly follows Capossere's line 'we shift immediately into a wholly different voice and tone:', exactly the location claimed. Sentence completes 'as of this morning. There should be sixty-six, but one has recently died and not yet been replaced' — present tense, dated to that morning. Page header confirms the review is by Bill Capossere for Fantasy Literature, reproduced with permission, of Children of Earth and Sky.

verdicts.trueWording: often employing passive voice, as we’re informed that the Rector’s Palace
verdicts.note: Same page, the paragraph immediately following that block quotation: 'This section goes on for several pages in this same wide-casting vision, often employing passive voice, as we’re informed that the Rector’s Palace has been rebuilt twice, that a subset of the population… dislike paying their taxes…' All four limbs (several pages; passive voice; civic facts; Palace rebuilt twice) are on the page in Capossere's own voice.
